name: Hochberg & Visser, 'The null energy condition in dynamic wormholes', PRL 81, 746 (1998); arXiv gr-qc/9802048v3: NEC violated or marginal on each of the two dynamic throats, strictly violated on an open region near each, and the transverse-averaged NEC violated on an open interval

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/9802048v3 (17 Feb 1998, revised 30 Apr 1998, v3 18 Jun 1998), full text, all 4 pages; companion gr-qc/9802046v2 (ref. [11], PRD 58, 044021) pp.1,4,11-21,25,29-30 read for the proof the Letter defers ('See [11,14] for details')

published_statement: Abstract: 'violations of the null energy condition (NEC) are a generic and universal feature of traversable wormholes ... [extended] to completely non-symmetric time-dependent wormholes ... phrased purely in terms of local geometry at and near the wormhole throat ... time-dependent wormholes have two throats, one for each direction through the wormhole, and ... the two throats coalesce only for the case of a static wormhole.' Central results: '(1) A time-dependent traversable wormhole will have two throats ... (2) For each one of these throats the NEC is either violated or on the verge of being violated on the throat itself. (3) For each one of these throats there will be an open region (topologically open in one of the null hypersurfaces passing through the throat) whose closure intersects the throat such that the NEC is violated throughout the open region. (4) For each one of these throats there will be an open interval such that the transverse averaged NEC (transverse averaged over the throat after it is pushed out in the appropriate null direction) is violated throughout the open interval.' Eq.(8) T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 on the throat; eq.(13) T_ab l^a l^b < 0 on an open neighbourhood near the throat; '(4) follows from appropriate modifications of the integrated constraint Eq.(11). See [11,14] for details.' Discussion: 'the suspension of the NEC is essentially an illusion in that if one ever succeeds in passing through the wormhole and reaching the other universe then one must have passed a throat as defined above and there must be NEC violations at or near this throat.'
published_hypotheses: H1 classical 3+1 spacetime with the Einstein equations (used to pass from eq.(7) R_ab l l <= 0 to eq.(8) T_ab l l <= 0); the NEC statement is about the TOTAL stress-energy -- splitting it into 'exotic' + 'normal' parts is called 'semantic games' (Brans-Dicke, higher-derivative, dilaton, scalar-tensor: the violation sits in the effective total source)
H2 the throat Sigma is a compact, orientable, two-sided, spacelike 2-surface embedded in spacetime, with the two orthogonal null geodesic congruences l_pm defined on an open neighbourhood

H3 throat w.r.t. l_pm: A[Sigma] > 0 and A[Sigma(u)] >= A[Sigma] for all deformation functions u(x) in an open neighbourhood of u = 0 (eq.3), giving theta_pm = 0 (eq.4) and pointwise null flare-out dtheta_pm/du_pm >= 0 everywhere on Sigma (eq.5) -- a NULL, not spatial, flare-out

H4 for the strict results (3),(4): the strict-increase condition eq.(9), A[Sigma(eps f)] > A[Sigma] for at least one f and eps in (-delta,0) U (0,delta), which excludes apparent horizons and bifurcation 2-spheres

H5 for result (4): the averaged flare-out condition of footnote [14] -- 'outward-flaring over at least half its area', formulated invariantly under affine reparametrisation; defined in the companion [11] def. 4.1.3 as int sqrt(gamma) sgn(dtheta/du) d^2x > 0; the 'transverse averaged NEC' is then [11] eq.(53) int sqrt(gamma) sgn(T_ab l^a l^b) d^2x < 0
H6 twist omega = 0 (automatic for a hypersurface-orthogonal congruence), shear-squared >= 0; smoothness sufficient for the Raychaudhuri equation (1) and the fundamental theorem of calculus
H7 the NEC conclusion is for the SAME null congruence that defines the throat (one direction per throat)

H8 the traversal step of the Discussion ('if one ever succeeds in passing through the wormhole ... one must have passed a throat as defined above') is ASSERTED, not proved; no asymptotic flatness, symmetry or causality assumption is made anywhere
hypothesis_drift: MERGED/STRENGTHENED (foliation.py:246-247): 'gr-qc/9802048: NEC violation on an open interval at any throat.' The source's OPEN-INTERVAL statement is result (4), and it is about the TRANSVERSE-AVERAGED NEC (a sgn-weighted area average, [11] eq.53), not pointwise NEC; the pointwise statement is result (3), and it is on an 'open region ... whose closure intersects the throat' in one null hypersurface -- 'at or near', not 'on an open interval at'. The line fuses (3) and (4) into a pointwise-on-an-interval claim the source does not make.

DROPPED (foliation.py:246-247 and driven.py:94-95, 895): the strict-increase condition eq.(9) (H4) and, for result (4), the averaged flare-out condition (H5, footnote [14] / [11] def.4.1.3). Under simple flare-out alone the source proves only (2): T_ab l l <= 0 on the throat, possibly = 0 ('on the verge'). 'At any throat' / 'around every throat' holds for throats satisfying H4 (results 3) and H4+H5 (result 4).

MIS-LISTED HYPOTHESIS (canonical entry, foliation.py): 'NEC' is listed as a hypothesis; in the source the NEC is the object of the CONCLUSION (it is violated), and no energy condition is assumed. The load-bearing hypothesis the list omits is the Einstein equations (H1) -- in any other gravity the conclusion is about the effective total source.

AMBIGUOUS WORDING (driven.py:895): 'the averaged NEC is violated on an open interval around every throat' -- without 'transverse' this reads as the ANEC; the companion [11] p.20 warns explicitly: 'this has nothing to do with the violation of the averaged null energy condition, or ANEC. In the ANEC, the averaging is defined to take place along inextendible null geodesics.' driven.py:94-95 has the correct word 'TRANSVERSE AVERAGED'.

ELIDED LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE (driven.py:96-98): the quotation '... if one ever succeeds in passing through the wormhole ... there must be NEC violations at or near this throat' drops, inside the ellipsis, 'and reaching the other universe then one must have passed a throat as defined above and'. That clause IS the hypothesis (H8): the NEC conclusion reaches a traversal only through the assertion that every traversal crosses a throat in H&V's null-minimal-surface sense, which the Letter does not prove. Maeda-Harada-Carr 0901.1153 and Tomikawa-Izumi-Shiromizu 1503.01926 exhibit dynamical cosmological wormholes (other throat definitions) with no such throat and with the dominant energy condition satisfied (machine-checked here, C7).

ADDED HYPOTHESIS (canonical entry, driven.py): 'traversability' is listed as a hypothesis of the theorem; the theorem's hypothesis is the existence of a throat (H2-H5); traversability enters only in the Discussion's asserted link (H8).

SCOPE EXTENSION (driven.py:311-312 and standard_table row at driven.py:517-518, 'therefore the corridor needs no negative energy' -- REFUTED -- 'Hochberg & Visser 1998; Olum 1998'): H&V's theorem concludes NEC violation at WORMHOLE THROATS (compact marginally anti-trapped 2-surfaces with null flare-out). The tree's corridor is a contraction region (Gamma > 1 in Misner-Sharp language); it is covered by H&V only if it contains a sphere with theta_+ = 0 (U + Gamma = 0 in foliation.py's own D5 form) or theta_- = 0 together with null flare-out, which driven.py does not show. What H&V do supply for the corridor is the methodological point of the companion's section 7 / the Letter's Discussion (spatial flare-out does not imply null flare-out), which driven.py:297 correctly calls 'the same point, arrived at from the other end'. For the corridor the refutation is carried by Olum (gr-qc/9805003), which the file itself calls 'the one that governs the project' -- not audited here.

WORDING 'negative energy' (driven.py:311-312, 517): the source concludes NEC violation, T_ab l^a l^b < 0. That implies a WEC violation -- some timelike observer measures negative energy density -- by continuity (checked, C6), but not negative energy density in every frame, nor a negative total or Misner-Sharp mass. The inference is sound in the observer-dependent sense only.

DISCREPANCY IN THE SOURCE'S SKETCH (not in the tree, recorded because the tree cites result (4)): the Letter's step eq.(10) -> eq.(11) writes d^2A/deps^2 > 0 as int sqrt(gamma) f^2 dtheta/du > 0; the second variation is int sqrt(gamma) f^2 (dtheta/du + theta^2) (computed, C4; the companion [11] eq.33 keeps theta^2 and drops it only ON the throat where theta = 0). Off the throat (eps != 0) theta != 0, so (10) alone does not give (11): a two-generator toy has A'' > 0 with int f^2 sqrt(g) theta' < 0 at the same eps (C4b). The toy violates the per-generator minimum eq.(3) (C4c), so it is NOT a counterexample to the theorem -- it shows eq.(3), not (9)/(10), must carry the step, and the Letter does not show that. Also, [11] p.15 states weighted averages of the eq.(11) form 'are too subject to reparameterization effects to be useful' (C3c) and proves the averaged result by the sgn-average instead. And the parenthetical '(in general (-delta2,0) U (0,+delta2))' after eq.(10) is not general for smooth A: a C-infinity A with A(eps) > A(0) has A'' of both signs arbitrarily near 0 (C5); the set {A'' > 0} accumulates at 0, which is all the argument needs. A misprint-level discrepancy in a sketch, NOT a refutation; the proof of (4) in the Letter is a sketch and the tree does not rely on the sketch.

data_at_publication.quantity: no measured input: a pure geometric theorem (Raychaudhuri equation + Einstein equations + throat definition). The only constant entering is the gravitational coupling 8piG in G_ab = 8piG T_ab, and only its SIGN matters
data_at_publication.value_now: G = 6.67430(15)e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 (CODATA 2018/2022 recommended value, NOT read at source in this audit); positivity is not in question
data_at_publication.source_now: not read here -- stated only to record that no datum is load-bearing; the conclusion depends on sign(G) alone
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: no -- the conclusion is sign(T_ab l l) = -sign(R_ab l l)/sign(G) evaluated on flare-out; any G > 0 gives the same sign; the theorem uses no other number

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (16 checks, sympy 1.14.0 + z3 get_version_string 5.1.0). C1: from the general spherically symmetric double-null metric, G_{++} = -(2/r)(r_{,++} + f_{,+} r_{,+}) and on theta_+ = 0, dtheta_+/dxi_+ = -G_{++}: null flare-out <=> T_{++} <= 0 (results (1)-(2) in spherical symmetry, agreeing with Maeda-Harada-Carr eq.3.8); C1b: an expanding conformally-Ellis example has its theta_+ = 0 and theta_- = 0 spheres at distinct, symmetric, off-centre places (l = (-3 +- sqrt 8)/2 vs (3 +- sqrt 8)/2 for b0 = 1/2), coalescing at l = 0 when static -- the Letter's 'two throats ... not at the center of symmetry'. C2 (z3): theta = 0, omega = 0, sigma^2 >= 0, dtheta/du >= 0 => R_ll <= 0, and strict flare-out => R_ll < 0 (negations UNSAT; vacuity guard SAT). C3 (z3, n = 6 points, a finite box): averaged flare-out ([11] def.4.1.3) => sgn-averaged NEC strictly violated ([11] eq.53) (negation UNSAT; guard SAT); C3c the non-sgn weighted average takes both signs under per-generator affine rescaling, as [11] p.15 says. C4: second area variation carries f^2(theta' + theta^2) -- the Letter's (10)->(11) omits theta^2 off the throat; C4b/c toy shows (10) alone does not give (11) but the toy violates eq.(3). C5: C-infinity A = exp(-1/|eps|)(2 + sin(1/eps^2)) has A'' of both signs in every (0, delta) (at eps ~ 3.989e-3, A'' = -1.36e-94 and +1.35e-94). C6: NEC violation => WEC violation for some timelike observer. C7: Maeda-Harada-Carr eqs (4.58)-(4.60) reproduced from the metric; for t0 <= b the NEC (radial and tangential) holds everywhere, and theta_+ theta_- t^2 = (b^2 - t0 x + x^2)(b^2 + t0 x + x^2)/(b^2+x^2)^2 > 0 for t0 < 2b, so there is no H&V throat -- consistent with the theorem, outside its class.

later_literature.ref: Hochberg & Visser, gr-qc/9802046 (PRD 58, 044021, 1998) -- the Letter's ref. [11]
later_literature.what: Supplies the definitions the Letter defers: simple / strong / strongly anti-trapped / averaged (sgn) / f-weighted / N-fold degenerate flare-out (Table 1). Proves (50) T_ll <= 0 on a simply flared throat, (51) strict at some point for strong flare-out, (52) everywhere for strongly anti-trapped, (53) int sqrt(g) sgn(T_ll) < 0 under AVERAGED flare-out -- so result (4) holds under a flare-out hypothesis the tree never states. Warns that the transverse average is not the ANEC. Its sec.6 conformal example (eqs 75-77) shows the suspension of the NEC and the loss of flare-out are the same condition.

Confirms the theorem inside its definition (eq.3.8: dtheta_+/dxi_+ = -8piG T_++ on theta_+ = 0, so NEC violated at every H&V and Hayward throat; a Hayward throat is necessarily an H&V throat). Narrows its REACH: 'the Hochberg-Visser and Hayward definitions miss an important class of dynamical wormhole spacetimes, namely cosmological wormholes'; throats as minimal spheres on SPACELIKE hypersurfaces may sit in trapped regions with no trapping horizon and 'there may be no violation of the energy conditions'. Analytic example ds^2 = -dt^2 + (t/t0)^2[dx^2 + (x^2+b^2)dOmega^2] satisfies the DEC for t0 <= b and is trapped everywhere for t0 < 2b (re-derived here, C7). Traversal between the two Friedmann regions is not demonstrated in that paper.

later_literature.ref: Tomikawa, Izumi & Shiromizu, 'New definition of wormhole throat', arXiv:1503.01926 (2015)
later_literature.what: Hybrid definition k = theta_+ - theta_- = 0 with flare-out r^a grad_a k > 0 and a timelike throat sequence as 'traversable'. Recovers NEC violation for static cases and FLRW candidates (eq.43), but the dynamical Ellis wormhole in an FLRW background satisfies the dominant energy condition in a time window, at about the Hubble radius (eqs 62-65); the authors add that small wormholes 'seem hard or impossible to construct ... without violating the energy condition'. Bears on H&V's asserted traversal step (H8), not on the theorem. Their critique of Maeda et al.: the spacelike-slice definition is slicing-dependent and admits de Sitter/FLRW.

Titles/abstract snippets only: modified-gravity wormholes (f(R), trace-extended, Harko-Lobo et al. 1301.6878) keep the matter NEC by moving the violation into the effective geometric source -- exactly the Letter's 'semantic games' class (H1), not a counterexample to the total-source statement; AdS/entanglement traversable wormholes (2501.02324) concern quantum ANEC violation. None read; no claim is taken from them.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The result takes NO measured input: it is a theorem from the Raychaudhuri equation, the Einstein equations (only sign(G) > 0 enters) and a definition of throat. So there is no datum the authors could have lacked that would move its conclusion, and none has moved (data_at_publication). What came later is not data but DEFINITIONAL scope: Maeda-Harada-Carr (2009) and Tomikawa-Izumi-Shiromizu (2015) show that in cosmological backgrounds with an initial singularity -- a setting the 1998 Letter's intuition ('if one ever succeeds in passing through ... one must have passed a throat as defined above') did not address -- there are dynamical wormholes, by other definitions, without an H&V throat and satisfying the DEC (reproduced here, C7). EVIDENCE AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result: the theorem itself is re-derived (C1, C2, C3) and later work confirms it inside its definition (MHC eq.3.8). EVIDENCE FOR a narrower reading: the traversal => H&V-throat link is asserted, not proved, and is contested by the later constructions, and the Letter's printed sketch of (4) has a gap (theta^2 dropped off the throat; C4) that the companion paper closes only by adopting a sgn-averaged flare-out hypothesis. Whether the MHC/TIS backgrounds describe the actual universe (accelerating, dark-energy dominated) is a datum question not checked here; it would bear on the reach of the Discussion sentence, not on the theorem. None of this touches the tree's corridor: the corridor is outside H&V's class in either direction unless it contains a null-flared marginally (anti-)trapped sphere.
grade_evidence: The theorem STANDS as published inside its definitions: results (1)-(2) re-derived symbolically in spherical symmetry (C1, C1b) and as a sign implication in general (C2, z3 UNSAT); result (4) in the companion's form ([11] eq.53) machine-checked from averaged flare-out (C3, z3 UNSAT, n = 6 box); later literature confirms it within its class (MHC 0901.1153 eq.3.8). No datum enters. It is NARROWED relative to the tree's USE: (a) foliation.py:246-247 fuses results (3) and (4) into 'NEC violation on an open interval at any throat' and drops the strict-increase hypothesis eq.(9) and, for (4), the averaged flare-out hypothesis (footnote [14], [11] def.4.1.3); (b) driven.py:895 'averaged NEC' without 'transverse' collides with ANEC, which [11] p.20 explicitly disclaims; (c) driven.py:96-98 elides the clause 'one must have passed a throat as defined above', the asserted, unproved link from traversal to an H&V throat -- later constructions (MHC 2009, TIS 2015) have dynamical wormholes without such a throat that satisfy the DEC (C7); (d) driven.py:311-312/517-518 extend the theorem as a refutation to a contraction corridor not shown to contain a throat; Olum carries that row, not H&V. Recorded as discrepancies, not refutations: the Letter's (10)->(11) step omits theta^2 off the throat (C4) and its '(in general (-delta2,0) U (0,delta2))' is not general for smooth A (C5); neither refutes a stated result. Not WRONG: no counterexample to any of results (1)-(4) under the published hypotheses was found or shown.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restates the use as 'for each throat satisfying eqs.(3),(9) [and, for (4), the averaged flare-out of [11] def.4.1.3], the NEC is violated on an open region of the null hypersurface whose closure meets the throat, and the transverse (sgn-)averaged NEC is violated on an open interval', keeps 'transverse', restores the elided clause as a named hypothesis, and either shows the corridor contains a null-flared theta_pm = 0 sphere or cites the corridor row to Olum alone. To WRONG: a smooth spacetime satisfying the Einstein equations and eqs.(3),(5),(9) in which T_ab l^a l^b >= 0 on a full neighbourhood of Sigma in the l-null hypersurface -- none is known, and C2/C3 show none exists for results (2) and the [11]-form of (4). To OPEN for result (4) specifically: if the open-interval (pushed-out) form, rather than the on-throat [11] eq.(53) form, were load-bearing, since neither document prints its proof.
